title: DLC Tileset for a time travel game in MZ

posts.author: Dodaro
posts.body: I want to make a time travel game in MZ for personal use. Can you recommend me some DLC tilesets, which I can use?(preferrably with characters, monsters and music) The game's structure will be similar to Chrono Trigger and LIVE A LIVE, there will be a lot of different eras from the stone age to a distant future (futuristic, maybe cyberpunk, not dystopic) and I want to buy a tileset pack with which I can make all of them (it can be multiple packs too if they match). It can be in any style, I like pixel art, but RTP extensions are fine too, the only thing that matters is consistency. Also if possible I only want to pay at most 20-30$ (there's currently a big sale on KOMODO Plaza too).

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Welcome!
As a tip, you will get more and better responses if you give your post some basic formatting. Many people will not bother to read a big block of text.
You're going to need to be more specific - what's wrong with the tilesets that come with RPG Maker? They have natural settings, medieval, and modern/future. How do you need your recommendations to be different?
Have you looked at the available products in the store? Most tilesets do not come with characters, and I don't think I've seen any that come with enemies or music. Your price expectation is also not realistic - most tilesets sell for 10-20 dollars, so getting a lot of different things for $30 isn't going to happen.
Have you browsed the many threads of free resources in the Resource section of the forum?

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
I think you could do it with Time Fantasy sets with how cheap they go when they're on sale. You also get seven years' worth of tilesets and graphic assets if you pay for a month of the creator's Patreon.
From a cost-value perspective it can't be beat, the downside is Time Fantasy is kinda overused due to how long it's been around and how cheap it is.
The other low-cost options are RTP/edits from any of the older RPG Makers or OpenGameArt/LPC collections
